chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Yaʿfūr narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “There is no spending more beloved to Allah than moderate spending, and He dislikes extravagance except in hajj or ʿumrah.”
ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about moderation in spending and extravagance in hajj or ʿumrah?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that Allah loves moderation in spending and dislikes extravagance. It makes an exception for hajj and ʿumrah, where greater expenditure is not condemned. The narration promotes financial balance while highlighting the special status of these acts of worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2446 - Abdullah ibn Abi Ya‘fur narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family) said:
"There is no spending more beloved to Allah (swt) than moderate spending. He dislikes extravagance, except in Hajj or Umrah."
